construct: Monopsony employment restriction and gains from additional hiring
why: The stem supplies both intersections, wages, MFC and MRP. The gap between monopsony and competitive employment is already specified, so the marginal social-gain explanation requires no figure.
repair: Leave both employment outcomes and the supply/MRP comparison to the graph; require a graph-specific employment interval together with the explanation that wages are transfers and forgone mutually beneficial hires reduce surplus.

construct: Specific versus general results of simultaneous labor-demand and supply shifts
why: Only the key permits offsetting wage effects or distinguishes an unchanged wage in this case from a universal rule. The other choices deny simultaneous shifts, fix employment by law, or contradict derived demand.
repair: Keep at least two theoretically possible final wages/employment changes, distinguished by the intersections; retain an incorrect claim that the actual offset must occur in every case.

construct: Lorenz shares, relative versus absolute income, Gini interpretation and proportional invariance
why: The question either asks a general definition/limitation of Lorenz curves and Gini, supplies the lower-Gini direction, or states every income share and total needed for the calculation.
repair: Require a particular curve or cumulative share to be read, then retain the inequality, group-mean, proportional-invariance or relative-versus-absolute interpretation. Use two plausible share calculations and an actual-value option with the wrong economic inference.

construct: Cumulative income shares versus population shares and Lorenz dominance
why: Only the key distinguishes population from income correctly, or explains Gini ordering through one Lorenz curve lying entirely below another. The other explanations confuse dollars and percentages, reverse the complement, or use irrelevant endpoints/means.
repair: Keep two valid income-share calculations at different readings, or two named curve orderings with coherent Gini implications; retain the actual reading paired with the relevant misconception.

construct: Gains from exchange measured as total surplus
why: Both full demand and supply equations are given. Their intersection and the total-surplus area follow without the graph.
repair: Obtain an intercept or equilibrium from the figure and retain interpretation of gains above resource cost; avoid merely asking for the coordinates.

construct: Distribution of gains from trade and positive net national surplus
why: Only the key has welfare components that sum consistently and a positive net gain from opening a standard small-country market. The others claim losses or unchanged total surplus despite stated gains exceeding losses.
repair: Offer two arithmetically consistent, economically possible trade/welfare packages with different graph-derived quantities and areas, plus the correct magnitudes with a reversed distributional interpretation.

construct: Private versus social incentives, optimal correction, social marginal equality and public-good underprovision
why: The stem asks the definition of an externality correction/efficient outcome, supplies the corrective direction or full versus partial correction, or gives both private and social provision levels. The textbook principle selects the key without any plotted evidence.
repair: Require the particular private/social intersection, residual marginal gap or benefit comparison from the graph, together with the reason the policy corrects or fails to correct incentives. Preserve the distinction between social gains and transfers.

construct: Corrective-policy calibration, welfare gains, public-good provision and marginal decision rules
why: Only the keyed alternative consistently applies marginal social benefit/cost and treats transfers separately from real costs. Alternatives assume any policy size works, a cap forces expansion, positive total benefit guarantees efficiency, terminal MC applies to every added unit, or transfers are resource gains/losses. The numerical content can be skipped.
repair: Retain at least two economically coherent policies/net-gain calculations with different graph-based marginal gaps, quantities or areas. Include the actual graph values attached to the targeted interpretation error, so both graph evidence and economics remain necessary.

construct: Tax revenue equals the tax per unit times taxed transactions
why: Both the $2 tax and 160-thousand quantity are in the stem; multiplication gives the key.
repair: Require reading the taxed quantity from the figure and applying the per-unit-tax times post-tax-transactions rule. Offer two plausible readings with that rule and the actual readings under a wrong tax-revenue calculation.

construct: Buyer price and seller receipt under a subsidy
why: The task explicitly asks for the policy wedge. Only B has buyers paying less than sellers receive; the other choices reverse the subsidy or remove its wedge.
repair: Use two buyer/seller pairs with the correct subsidy direction and different plotted price levels, plus the observed pair with the wrong incidence interpretation.
